rect.title: header length in 32-bit words; min 5 (=20 bytes), max 15 (=60 bytes)
receive window size in bytes (subject to window scaling option)
0-320 bits (0-40 octets), always a multiple of 32, padded to a 32-bit boundary — RFC 9293 §3.1
variable-length payload; length derived from the IP datagram, not carried in the TCP header

g.text: Width is VARIABLE on the wire; the declared width is one representative word, not the field's length

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 bitfield # TCP Header — RFC 9293 §3.1, IETF MSB-0 bit numbering (bit 0 = leftmost). # The .fd is the machine-readable truth: field ORDER + WIDTH give every # bit its absolute offset, so a reader answers "which bits carry X?" from # text alone — no pixels, no OCR. title "TCP Header"
class varword "Width is VARIABLE on the wire; the declared width is one representative word, not the field's length"
bitfield tcp "TCP Header (RFC 9293)" word=32 numbering=msb0
# Row 1: Source Port (16) + Destination Port (16) = 32 bits field "Source Port" 16 field "Destination Port" 16
# Row 2: Sequence Number = 32 bits field "Sequence Number" 32
# Row 3: Acknowledgment Number = 32 bits field "Acknowledgment Number" 32
# Row 4: Data Offset (4) + Reserved (4) + 8 control flags (1 bit each) + Window (16) field "Data Offset" 4 description="header length in 32-bit words; min 5 (=20 bytes), max 15 (=60 bytes)" field "Reserved" 4 description="must be zero" # The eight control bits are declared as individual 1-bit fields so a reader # can address each flag's exact bit position, not just the byte that holds them. # The first six use the COMPACT form: `name:width` pairs, comma-separated on one # `field` line, declare exactly the same six one-bit fields the long form would — # same model, same boxes, six lines saved. The compact form takes no option keys, # so SYN and FIN stay long-form: they carry a `fill=` that marks the two flags # this figure is highlighting. field CWR:1,ECE:1,URG:1,ACK:1,PSH:1,RST:1 field "SYN" 1 fill=#fee2e2 field "FIN" 1 fill=#fee2e2 field "Window" 16 description="receive window size in bytes (subject to window scaling option)"
# Row 5: Checksum (16) + Urgent Pointer (16) = 32 bits field "Checksum" 16 field "Urgent Pointer" 16
# Row 6+: Options — the dashed border marks conditional presence, and the # condition itself is now in the model and drawn as a caption; a reader # computing offsets past here MUST branch (`BITFIELD-CONDITIONAL-OFFSETS`). The WIDTH is 0-320 bits # (0-40 octets) on the wire: v0.1 has no range width (`BITFIELD-RANGE-WIDTH`) and `*` is # spent on Data, so 32 is one representative word, said in the class meaning. field "Options" 32 present="Data Offset > 5" class=varword description="0-320 bits (0-40 octets), always a multiple of 32, padded to a 32-bit boundary — RFC 9293 §3.1"
# Payload — variable length, inferred from the IP total length, not a TCP field field "Data" * description="variable-length payload; length derived from the IP datagram, not carried in the TCP header"
